text:
Tampa Bay won 4-1, but the score undersells how lopsided this was. The Lightning generated 5.11 expected goals to Philadelphia's 1.85, and out-attempted the Flyers 70 to 37. Replay every shot a thousand times and TBL wins 84 percent of them. Neither team scored on the power play (0 for 3 each), so almost all of that gap came at even strength, where Tampa Bay held a 3.07 to 1.17 edge in chance quality.

The goals arrived on modest looks. Brayden Point tipped one in late in the first period, and Pontus Holmberg made it 2-0 seventeen seconds into the second. Tyson Foerster answered at 7:22 with a wrist shot, rated about a 5 percent chance, and for a stretch Philadelphia was hanging on to a one-goal deficit despite being outplayed. Tampa kept pressing anyway, piling up 1.17 expected goals in the middle period against 0.91 for the Flyers, their closest frame.

The third period ended the argument. Tampa Bay posted 2.29 expected goals to 0.61, and Ilya Mikheyev finished a wrap-around at 17:00 before Brandon Hagel added a high-quality chance (89 percent) with seven seconds left to make it 4-1. Hagel was the engine, taking eight shots with 1.59 individual expected goals. Dan Vladar faced 35 shots for Philadelphia and stopped about 1.2 goals more than expected, which kept it close for as long as it was. Andrei Vasilevskiy saw only 15 shots and allowed one.
